items.description: Turn BloodHound attack path exports into dual-layer security reports — CISO executive prose on top, technical remediation playbook below. Automates Active Directory audit reporting for pentesters, blue teams, and security consultants. Supports DCSync, Kerberoasting, AD CS abuse (ESC1/3/4/6/7/9/10/13, Golden Certificate), resource-based constrained delegation, shadow credentials, LAPS and gMSA password reads, ACL abuse, GPO takeover, and lateral movement paths. Pure local PowerShell — no API calls, no data leaves your machine. Air-gap compatible.

latestVersion.changelog:
Fixes twelve edge types that were silently scored as zero — GenericWrite, WriteOwner, AllExtendedRights, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, ReadLAPSPassword, ReadGMSAPassword, GpLink, AdminTo, HasSession and others. Paths built from these alone previously reported as Low. Restores remediation guidance to Tier 0 findings, which rendered with an empty remediation section. Hardens against malformed pwdlastset values and edges referencing missing nodes, both of which aborted the run. Caps scores at 100.

Adds AD CS detection (ESC1, ESC3, ESC4, ESC6a/b, ESC7, ESC9a/b, ESC10a/b, ESC13, Golden Certificate, CA management rights, PKI template flag writes), resource-based constrained delegation, shadow credentials, LAPS and gMSA password reads, and additional lateral movement edges — each with dedicated remediation guidance.

Tier 0 now weighted in two bands: core groups score above operator groups. Kerberoastable accounts detected anywhere in a path, not only at the source. Unrecognised edge labels are reported rather than scored as zero, so newer BloodHound schemas no longer understate severity silently.

Severity output for the bundled fixtures is unchanged from 1.0.1, enforced by a regression test. Paths relying on previously-unscored edges will rate higher than on 1.0.1 — note the tool version in deliverables and re-baseline before comparing assessments.

Not for CI pipeline YAML (github-actions, gitlab) or for composing the pull request description itself (pull-request).

items.summary: Curates news, feeds, and industry sources into personalized recurring digests: sourcing, filtering, ranking, and delivery. Use to set up a daily briefing or morning/evening news roundup, track competitors, an industry, people, or markets, or run a scheduled or weekly update. Also when a digest feels too long or repetitive, keeps missing stories, or a rumor needs checking before it ships. Covers source vetting, deduplication, single-source holds, corrections, urgent alerts, slow news days, and channel formats (email, Slack, Telegram, audio); learns format, timing, and depth preferences from reactions. Not for summarizing documents the user provides or internal business reporting.
